net/failure#

What went wrong with a connection, as one kind code takes it apart by.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

catch NetworkFailure.detailed(kind, operation, code, message) { if kind == NetworkFailureKind.refused { … } }

Description#

What went wrong with a connection, as one kind code takes it apart by.

NetworkError turns a runtime failure into that error.

object NetworkError#

object NetworkError

A normalized native failure at an explicitly named network boundary. Binding is effect-free; applicable() distinguishes terminal core.net failures. Catch only NativeFailure around that boundary, then:

let translated = NetworkError(NetworkOperation.connecting, failure);
if translated.applicable() {throw translated.value();}
throw; // bare rethrow in the original catch preserves NativeFailure

Only core.net is translated. Foreign domains, would_block and interrupted are inapplicable. The last two belong to the poll/retry loop; this adapter neither retries nor classifies them as terminal network failures. value() on an inapplicable failure throws InvalidArgument. The original catch owns the bare rethrow; a NativeFailure value cannot be thrown as an Error. Native timed_out returns async/timeout.TimedOut. Already-thrown Cancelled and TimedOut never enter a NativeFailure catch and remain unchanged.

Known portable categories map exactly; other codes map to other, preserving message() byte-for-byte as text. No message/symbol heuristics or host codes. The current provider merges aborted into connection_reset; do not invent the lost distinction. Legacy aborted/timed_out enum members remain valid for manual NetworkFailure construction. Returned NetworkFailure owns only public values.

Errors#

enum NetworkFailure#

enum NetworkFailure is Error = (detailed(operation is NetworkOperation, kind is NetworkFailureKind, message is string))

Immutable observation: attempted operation, portable kind and exact diagnostic. No I/O, parsing of message text, locale rules or resource lifecycle. Empty and Unicode diagnostics are valid. Existing constructor and enum values are stable.

throw NetworkFailure.detailed(NetworkOperation.reading,
    NetworkFailureKind.reset, "connection was reset");
catch NetworkFailure.detailed(operation, kind, message) { ... }
